source_text.body:
Run websites, reports and listings with OpenClaw
Commenters use OpenClaw to build websites, notify when kids arrive home, run WooCommerce reports to SharePoint, and manage a willhaben account with postings, price research and replies.
·
Aug 2, 2026
Done with
OC
OpenClaw
What they did
In this Reddit thread, several commenters describe giving OpenClaw direct access to systems they already run and then steering it with prompts. One runs the same agent in a home-lab VM, handing it Linux, a public IP, and needed keys so it can build websites while they troubleshoot; others mention wiring it to Teams for WooCommerce reporting into SharePoint, using it for a home/away tracker that notifies when kids arrive, and having it handle willhaben listings by researching prices, undercutting, posting, and flagging incoming messages.
How it went
The source gives practical examples but almost no hard metrics. The clearest limits are that keeping the agent alive was a challenge for the website builder, and the other commenters describe workflows and convenience rather than measured business results.
Worth knowing
You still need to supply the environment and permissions yourself, and at least one user says the ongoing burden is paying for it and troubleshooting it.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
Set up a recurring job for me: every [day/time], pull [data source, e.g. WooCommerce orders] into a short report and save it to [destination, e.g. SharePoint folder]. Also message me on [chat app] when [event, e.g. my kids get home]. Done means one successful test run of each, and before you send anything to anyone besides me or change my accounts, show me what you plan to do.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/openclaw/comments/1vdj4rg/interested_in_using_openclaw_and_trying_it_out
